title: Microcard components and thematic token library for compact dashboards
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Summary:
Create a suite of compact microcard UI components and a paired thematic token library to support high-density dashboards, rollout controls, and cost-insight panels in the Redwood Console. The goal is a small, reusable component set (microcard, micro-metric-row, compact-chip, condensed-avatar) plus a token map (spacing, typography, elevation, color variants) that enables 3 density modes (comfortable, compact, dense) across light/dark themes while preserving accessibility and clear visual hierarchy.

Context and motivation:
- Problems observed in Console: several dashboard pages have inconsistent spacing, duplicated ad-hoc card styles, and poor behavior at narrow widths. Rollout controls and cost tiles currently have bespoke implementations leading to developer friction and visual regressions.
- Objective: reduce variations by providing a single source of truth (Figma library + token map) and a set of tiny, composable components for metric-heavy pages. Aim for an initial adoption in Cost Insights and Model Rollouts.

Scope and deliverables:
- Figma component library: Microcard (3 sizes), MicroMetricRow, CompactStatusChip, MicroAvatar, MiniProgressBar, Skeleton variants.
- Thematic token file: spacing scale (s-1..s-6), type scale (micro, small, base), elevation tokens for 2 levels of shadow, color tokens for success/warn/error/neutral with WCAG contrast for small text.
- Documentation pages: usage guidelines, density migration notes, code examples for token mapping (CSS variables naming convention: --rdw-*) and component props for density/theme.
- Prototype links and handoff assets for frontend engineers.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Density modes: Instead of inventing new token names per density, we map logical tokens to density variants (e.g., spacing.s-2 -> 8px in comfortable, 6px in compact, 4px in dense). This keeps semantic tokens in code while enabling theme overrides.
- Typography: maintain minimum readable font-size for micro mode at 12px with strong contrast and avoid reducing below 12px to preserve legibility.
- Touch targets: microcards intended primarily for desktop dashboards; interactive touch targets (buttons in microcards) must maintain 40px min tappable area — we use overlay affordances for mobile.
- Performance: prefer single-layer shadows and 1px separators in dense mode to reduce compositing overhead on lower-end GPUs.

Prototype and links:
- Figma file (working): https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/rdw-microcards-tokens (working branch: /compact-dashboard-kit)
- Storybook mock (WIP): https://staging-console.redwood.ai/storybook/?path=/story/microcard
- GH PR for token CSS variables: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1824

Accessibility checklist:
- Contrast: tokens validated to meet AA large text and AA for small text where possible. Exceptions documented for tertiary labels with review notes.
- Keyboard: focus styles for microcard interactive elements match Console default but scaled to density.
- Screen readers: ensure micro-metric-row exposes role="list" and items expose labels via aria-label when truncated.

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma library contains all components with documented tokens and usage notes.
- Frontend implementation in Storybook matches Figma spec within 1px spacing and color deltas < 3% LAB.
- Migration guide for two pilot pages (Cost Insights and Rollouts) with before/after screenshots and checklist for QA.
- Accessibility audit completed and documented with remediation steps for any WCAG failures.

Implementation notes for engineers:
- Token naming convention: --rdw-spacing-s1 ... --rdw-type-micro ... --rdw-elevation-1. Density mapping will live in a single override CSS class (.rdw-density-compact, .rdw-density-dense).
- Provide CSS variables fallback to preserve behavior in older browser or SSR initial render.
- Suggested component props: density: ['comfortable','compact','dense'], theme: ['light','dark'], interactive: boolean.

Rollout plan:
1) Publish Figma library and sync with token JSON export (design -> tokens repo).
2) Implement Storybook components and add to Console component registry.
3) Pilot on Cost Insights (feature flag) and Rollouts page with QA signoff.
4) Gradual enablement across dashboards with a migration checklist for each page.

Notes on future work:
- Explore compact grid utilities for responsive rearrangement of microcards when width < 720px.
- Consider a density preference in user settings tied to Console account.
